title.rendered: Death and Life Are in the Power of the Tongue | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 3

excerpt.rendered: Proverbs 18:21 is not poetry, it is a courtroom. Your tongue is signing verdicts over your life every day. Day 3 shows how to speak life on purpose.

content.rendered:
Your tongue is not a passenger. It is a courtroom. Every careless sentence is a verdict signed over your own life, and heaven honours it, for life or for death.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, October 20, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 3

Today’s Scripture

“Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.”
Proverbs 18:21 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Proverbs 18:21 is one of the most quoted verses in the Bible, and still one of the least obeyed. The NKJV says, “Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.” The AMPC drives the warning home: “Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and they who indulge in it shall eat the fruit of it [for death or life].” The TPT is almost chilling: “Your words are so powerful that they will kill or give life, and the talkative person will reap the consequences.” Scripture is telling us that the tongue has power, not metaphorical power, but power that produces fruit.

From Lagos to London, Manila to Nairobi, São Paulo and beyond, believers are waking up to the uncomfortable fact that we have spoken many of our seasons into being. We prayed one way on Sunday and talked another way on Monday. The tongue is where private faith becomes public reality. In Lagos, a man curses his boss on the ride home and wonders why work feels like a prison. In London, a mother jokes that her son is “hopeless” and later weeps that he cannot find his way. In Manila and Nairobi and São Paulo, pastors warn their congregations: careless words are expensive words.

Jesus made the same point with surgical precision: “By your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned” (Matthew 12:37). He was not threatening us; He was teaching us. Words are seeds. Seeds have fruit. Fruit has flavour. If you have been eating a bitter season, examine the garden you have been planting. Repent of the deadly words, uproot them where you can, and begin again, this time, planting life.

Declaration is not just about getting miracles; it is about tending your own soul. “Those who love the tongue shall eat its fruit.” So love the tongue well. Train it. Treat your words the way a surgeon treats a scalpel, with reverence and intent. The believer who learns to speak life on purpose is a believer whose life slowly begins to taste like heaven.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. God Himself installed the law: words produce fruit. You cannot opt out of it. The question is not whether your tongue is building something, it is what it is building.

Personalise. Audit your mouth. What have you been saying about yourself, your spouse, your children, your work, your church, your nation? Confess what has been destructive. Agree with God and shift.

Proclaim. Speak life on purpose. Not naive positivity, scriptural life. Replace every careless sentence with a Spirit-sharpened one. “Let your speech always be with grace” (Colossians 4:6).

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that my tongue is subject to the Spirit of God. Death and life are in its power, and I choose life. I renounce every careless word I have spoken over my body, my family, my calling, my finances, and my future. I pull up those weeds by the root in the name of Jesus. From today, my mouth is a wellspring of life. I speak blessing where I used to speak doubt. I bless my family. I bless my work. I bless my city. I bless my enemies. I will eat the fruit of my tongue, and the fruit shall be sweet, because the words planting it are the words of the Lord. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
